fact: The report says Circulaire n°002/2020/CB/C of the UEMOA Banking Commission, in force since 18 September 2020, obliges credit institutions, microfinance institutions and electronic money institutions to run an internal customer-complaints system with a reply within one month.

The report says BCEAO Instruction n°001-01-2024 on payment services in the UEMOA requires electronic money issuers to operate complaint-handling systems for clients and merchants, with set resolution deadlines and tracking.

The report says decree 2022-1066 of 9 December 2022 created the Observatoire de la qualité des services financiers (OQSF-BF) with financial mediation between providers, including electronic money issuers, and users, and that the UEMOA Banking Commission can also be seized when a complaint is unsatisfied.
The report, citing BCEAO, says electronic money issuers in Burkina Faso recorded 4,200 complaints in 2022, with 85% resolved within the deadline.

The OQSF-BF, housed in the state agency ANPFI, mediates free of charge disputes with banks, microfinance institutions, insurers and e-money issuers, and says it has handled more than 220 cases since 2022 with about 92% settled amicably.
